## Introduction to GitHub Foundations (GH-900)

The GitHub Foundations is an introduction exam to GitHub. In short, GitHub is a shared website where you can store and share repositories with others and collaborate on them. This platform is designed for developers.

The objectives of the exam are on this day:

- Understand Git and GitHub basics (25–30%)

- Work with GitHub repositories (10–15%)

- Collaborate using GitHub (10–15%)

- Apply modern development practices (10–15%)

- Manage projects with GitHub (5–10%)

- Understand privacy, security, and administration (10–15%)

- Explore the GitHub community (5–10%)

[https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/credentials/certifications/resources/study-guides/gh-900#skills-at-a-glance-as-of-january-2026](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/credentials/certifications/resources/study-guides/gh-900#skills-at-a-glance-as-of-january-2026)

## Introduction to Git

Git is a system which manages versions of your code. We can call this a versioning system. As developers will work with code daily, and improper updates to code can break other features, we need versioning to quickly restore to a previous version. We can also make some documentation about what actually has happened with a new version.

<a class="btn btn-primary" href="https://git-scm.com/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer">Download Git</a>

Git is a tool which you can download on your computer and can be used to upload your code to GitHub, where the actual versioning will happen. An actual introduction to this program can be found here which is an exercise you can perform: [https://github.com/skills/introduction-to-git](https://github.com/skills/introduction-to-git)

## Introduction to GitHub

GitHub is a cloud platform where developers can share and collaborate on their code. It supports creating repositories, a logical container to share code of a particular project. The primary part of GitHub is Git, which we just described. The main components of GitHub are:

- Repositories
- Actions
- GitHub Pages

### Repository

A repository is a container where we can place all code of a particular project. The website where you read this on for example, is stored in [a GitHub repository](https://github.com/JustinVerstijnen/JVTechnicalBlog):

[![](data:image/png;base64,)](data:image/png;base64,)

Every repository can also contain a Wiki page, where you can create documentation of your project which is also really nice. All types of text in GitHub can be managed with Markdown, an easy markup language for readable text with syntaxes. You can find this wiki on the "Wiki" tab and start creating your own.

### Actions

GitHub Actions are automated tasks which you can run in a repository. For example to push your updated code to Microsoft Azure services like [Static Web Apps](https://justinverstijnen.nl/creating-static-web-apps-on-azure-the-easy-way/) or [mirror the code to another repository](https://justinverstijnen.nl/upload-multiple-github-repositories-into-a-single-azure-static-web-app/). Actions are based on the CI/CD workflow, where update of the code will result in a update on all services, making GitHub a single source of truth.

Actions are written in YAML code and are stored in the repository in the folder .github/workflows. Any action that is placed at that location will be run at an commit/update of the repository.

### GitHub Pages

GitHub Pages are websites that are run directly from a GitHub repository to the internet, [where the setup is relatively easy](https://justinverstijnen.nl/getting-started-with-github-pages/) and fast. This website is also running on GitHub Pages because it is working greatly. It is however limited to front-end code only, so HTML, CSS and Javascript. Server side code like PHP is not supported.

### Definitions

In Git and GitHub we have some general definitions which we will describe:

| Definition | Explaination |
| --- | --- |
| Commit | A commit is a save-action to your repository, effectively creating a new version of the code. Commits can also have a comment where the developer can add what has changed in the code |
| Pull request | A pull request is a signal to merge branches |
| Branches | Branches are designed to make changes without altering the actual code. This can be a copy of the code used for testing purposes |
| Releases | A release/version of your compiled code |
